statute_cards.title: General Construction Threshold
statute_cards.description: Florida law mandates an NOC for any improvement, repair, or alteration contract valued over $5,000.

statute_cards.title: Direct A/C & Mechanical Systems
statute_cards.description: The statutory threshold is increased to $15,000 for direct replacement of existing heating or air conditioning systems.

statute_cards.title: Mandatory Before 1st Inspection
statute_cards.description: Inspectors cannot perform underground, slab, or framing inspections unless a certified copy is on the job site.

steps.title: Complete County NOC Form
steps.description: Enter the exact legal property description, folio/parcel ID, owner name, lender details, and contractor credentials (Just Smart Choice Construction USA, Lic #CGC1534063).

steps.title: Notarize All Owner Signatures
steps.description: All deeded property owners must execute the document before a commissioned Florida Notary Public (or via Florida-approved Remote Online Notarization).

steps.title: Record with County Clerk of Court
steps.description: Submit the original notarized form to the Official Records department of your county clerk, either electronically via Simplifile/e-Recording or in person.

steps.title: Post Certified Copy at Job Site
steps.description: Keep the clerk's certified recorded copy posted inside the job site permit weather-box before the local municipal building inspector arrives.

faqs.question: What happens if a Florida project starts without an NOC?
faqs.answer: Building department inspectors will fail the very first inspection, issuing a red tag or stop-work notice until a certified recorded NOC is posted on site.

faqs.question: Can Just Smart Choice record the NOC for me?
faqs.answer: Yes. As part of our turnkey general contracting service, our permit expediting desk coordinates notarization, electronic recording, and site posting for all client projects.

faqs.question: How long is a Florida Notice of Commencement valid?
faqs.answer: Under F.S. § 713.13(1)(c), an NOC remains effective for one (1) year from the recording date unless an earlier or later expiration date is specifically stated on the form.
